      14             The network represents over

      18             Supportive housing; permanent, affordable

      19      housing link to on-site services is the proven

      20      cost-effective and humane way to provide stable

      21      homes to individuals and families who have

      22      difficult finding and maintaining housing.

      23             The people we house and serve -- people of

      24      mental illness, HIV/AIDS, substance abuse, and other

       1      users of expensive emergency services, like

       3      centers.

       4             Because placement into supportive housing has

       5      been proven to reduce use of these services, the

       6      housing saves taxpayers money, often far more

       7      than what was spend building, operating, and

       8      providing services in the housing.

       9             This has been proven time and time again by

      10      dozens of peer-reviewed academic studies.

      11             I'm here today to discuss the recent budget

      12      cuts that the on-site support services and

      13      supportive housing have endured over the past

      14      two years, and to ask for the Senate's support in

      15      restoring the funding to the OTDA New York State

      16      Supportive Housing Program.

      17             NYSHP is the mainstay of supportive housing.

      18      It pays for critical on-site services that make it

      19      possible to house multiply disabled and vulnerable

      20      individuals, families and children, in permanent,

      21      affordable apartments.

      22             NYSHP funds the housing-based support

      23      services for over 16,000 formerly homeless and

      24      at-risk single adults, families, and children, and

      25      youth throughout New York State.

       1             NYSHP supports three different

       2      service-funding streams: services for single

       3      adults, families and children, and young adults.

       4             The largest part of this funding is allocated

       5      for support services for single adults.

       6             For the past 30 years, every administration

       7      has steadily invested State capital dollars to build

       8      new supportive-housing units; then provided these

       9      necessary funding streams to pay for the essential

      10      services and operating costs when they open.

      11             They did this because they understood that an

      12      investment in supportive housing saves them money.

      13             Supportive housing has helped us close

      14      thousands of inpatient psychiatric beds, and has

      15      made a significant measurable dent in the number of

      16      disabled individuals living on our streets.
